This could include ticking a box when visiting an internet website, choosing technical settings for information society services or another statement or conduct which clearly indicates in this context the data subject's acceptance of the proposed processing of his or her personal data. final_report.overview: Under Directive 2002/58/EC, a preselected checkbox does not constitute valid consent because consent must be given by a clear affirmative act, and silence, pre-ticked boxes, or inactivity are insufficient. The directive does not require that the information stored or accessed via cookies be personal data for consent and information obligations to apply—these obligations arise from the act of storing or accessing information on terminal equipment, regardless of whether the data is personal. However, the retrieved legislation does not specify whether clear and comprehensive information must include cookie duration or third-party access; this cannot be established from the provided evidence alone. Temporally, Directive 95/46/EC applied to cookie-based processing until 25 May 2018, when it was repealed and replaced by the GDPR (Regulation EU 2016/679), while Directive 2002/58/EC remained in force alongside the GDPR after that date, with both applying to cookie-based processing.

sections.title: Validity of preselected checkbox as consent under Directive 2002/58/EC
sections.answer_text: No, a preselected checkbox cannot constitute valid consent for storing or accessing information on a user's terminal equipment under Directive 2002/58/EC, as consent must be given by a clear affirmative act and silence, pre-ticked boxes, or inactivity should not constitute consent.

sections.title: Requirement for information to be personal data under Directive 2002/58/EC
sections.answer_text: The provided evidence does not contain sufficient information from Directive 2002/58/EC to determine whether the information stored or accessed via cookies must be personal data for the consent and information obligations to apply. The directive's obligations arise from the act of storing or accessing information on terminal equipment, but the evidence does not confirm whether this applies irrespective of whether the data is personal.

sections.title: Content of clear and comprehensive information under Directive 2002/58/EC
sections.answer_text: The provided evidence does not contain any information about Directive 2002/58/EC, cookies, or the requirements for clear and comprehensive information about cookies, including details on cookie duration or third-party access. Therefore, it cannot be established from the retrieved legislation alone whether such details must be included.

sections.title: Temporal applicability of Directive 95/46/EC, GDPR, and Directive 2002/58/EC
sections.answer_text: Directive 95/46/EC was repealed and replaced by Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) with effect from 25 May 2018. Directive 2002/58/EC (ePrivacy Directive) remained in force alongside the GDPR after 25 May 2018, and both regulations apply to cookie-based processing, with the GDPR providing the general data protection framework and Directive 2002/58/EC specifying rules for electronic communications, including cookies. Before 25 May 2018, Directive 95/46/EC and Directive 2002/58/EC both applied to cookie-based processing.
